title: Learn the Mayfair Quickstep at home

method.teacher_system: The teachers introduce the dance and explain how it will be broken down into parts. They demonstrate the steps clearly with counts from a back-facing view so learners can mirror them, repeating sections multiple times before linking them together.

practices.what: Demonstrate the first section of walking steps forward and pointing, breaking down the footwork for leaders and followers.
Count out loud while walking and pointing through the first section of steps.
Review and repeat the first section of the sequence again from the beginning.
Teach the next section involving side-close-side steps and turns into the ballroom hold.
Review the previous sections combined and check on how the learners are getting on.
Teach the following turning section with side-close-side steps moving backwards and forwards.
Run through the accumulated sequence sections together with continuous counting and reminders.
Teach the final step-tap combination to return to the starting position.

moments.says: The teacher greets the viewers and introduces themselves before explaining the Mayfair Quickstep dance sequence.
The teacher outlines that the routine will be broken down into three manageable parts before putting it all together with music.
The teacher offers warm encouragement and positive reinforcement after completing a run-through of the steps.
The teacher checks in with the learners by asking how they managed with the specific sequence review.
The teacher humorously corrects a slip of the tongue about dance terminology, making light of the mistake with laughter.

mentor.what_stays: The teacher leaves the learner feeling encouraged, capable, and ready to enjoy practicing the sequence at home.

clicked.theme: Clear step-by-step breakdown and repetition helped cement the memory

meant.theme: Perfect for brushing up before a cruise or dance event

method.limits: Music is not included during the instructional sections in the first 10 minutes of the video.
